Lessons learned: (1) All limit changes require 72-hour advance notice. (2) Clients must have a documented escalation path. (3) Rate limit headers should be included in all API responses.
API versioning policy: breaking changes require a deprecation notice period of at least 30 days. Rate limit adjustments are considered breaking changes when they reduce the existing limit.

result.title: API Validation Rule — Updated Decision Record
result.content:
## Decision: API Payload Validation Rule (Updated)

### Previous Rule
All API inputs were validated against a JSON schema. Empty arrays in request payloads were **rejected** (returned HTTP 400).

### Updated Rule (Effective from this record)
All API inputs continue to be validated against a JSON schema. **Empty arrays in request payloads are now permitted.** A previously-rejected payload containing an empty array will pass validation and be processed normally.

### Rationale
Post-mortem analysis identified that the strict rejection of empty arrays caused unintended downstream failures for valid consumer use cases. Allowing empty arrays aligns the API contract more closely with real-world client behaviour and reduces unnecessary error noise.

### Consumer Notice Requirement
Per lessons learned from the post-mortem, **all API consumers must receive at least 72 hours advance notice** before any future validation rule changes take effect. This notice period is now a standing requirement for all subsequent validation amendments.

### Change Log
- 2024-11-01: Initial rule — empty arrays rejected.
- (Current update): Empty arrays permitted; 72-hour consumer advance-notice requirement introduced.
